questions.heading: Every Row Family Is a Table of (row, column, coefficient)
questions.stem: Project Q7 may start in 2029 or 2030 and costs 400, then 600, in its two years of work. After the start variables are joined to the cost rows, which budget entries does x[Q7,2030] get?

options.text: budget_2030: 600 and budget_2031: 400, since the profile runs back from the end
options.says: The profile runs forward from the start: k = 0 is the start year, so 2030 gets the first year's cost.

options.text: budget_2030: 1,000 only, since the join books the whole cost in the start year
options.says: The join pairs the variable with every cost row; each lands in year start + k, as in lesson 6.4.2.

options.text: budget_2030: 400 and budget_2031: 600, since year t + k gets the k-th year's cost
options.says: Right: the year a cost lands in is start + k, the key the budget family matches rows on.

options.text: budget_2029: 400 and budget_2030: 600, since each start pays from its window's first year
options.says: Each start variable pays from its own start year; the 2029 start would be the one paying in 2029.

questions.heading: Hand MathOpt the Whole Matrix as a ModelProto
questions.stem: A proto builder forgot to sort its matrix entries by row and column, and also gave two variables the same name. It calls Model.from_model_proto on the proto and then solves. Where does it first fail?

options.text: At loading, which refuses the unsorted entries with a ValueError
options.says: Right: entry order and ids are checked when the proto is loaded; names are checked only at solve time.

options.text: At solving, since loading sorts the entries and keeps both names
options.says: Loading does not sort: proto_rules.py's out-of-order row was refused with a ValueError.

options.text: Nowhere, since the solve quietly renames one of the two twins
options.says: Twin names are refused at solve time ('duplicate name inserted'); nothing renames them.

options.text: At loading, which refuses the twin names before any other check
options.says: The twin x loaded without complaint in proto_rules.py; names wait for the solve.

questions.heading: A Fast Builder Is Correct Only If Its Exported Model Equals the Slow One's
questions.stem: A new builder's exported ModelProto is not equal to the old builder's, yet comparing the two models by name lists no difference at all. What does that mean?

options.text: A coefficient bug, since a comparison by name skips every coefficient
options.says: The comparison by name includes every row's coefficients; it found the costs shifted a year late.

options.text: Different optima, since a solver reads variables in the order they were added
options.says: Order changes neither the feasible plans nor their values, so the optimum is the same.

options.text: A broken check, since unequal protos must always differ by some name
options.says: The year-first build had unequal protos and no difference by name: same model, other order.

options.text: The same model, since only the order of its variables or rows changed
options.says: Right: proto equality is strict about order, and a comparison by name leaves order out.
